summary: Delayed chat handshake and streaming slowdown after model + compiler cutover
description:
Issue summary: After the scheduled cutover of the inference compiler and pinning the dedicated customer's fleet to redwood-7b-quant-v2, SlateDocs reported elevated chat session startup latency. Impact: customers see 5–12s TTFB for the first streaming token; some sessions time out at 30s and retry logic triggers duplicate streams. Scope: affects ~8% of requests from the customer's dedicated pool in us-east following the 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC deployment. This appears correlated with the compiler handoff and model binary swap.

Observed user-facing symptoms: slow initial handshake, delayed first byte, intermittent 504s for chat streaming, and increased request duration tail.

Why this ticket exists: to capture support investigation, mitigation steps applied, and remediation plan for the customer and internal stakeholders.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a chat session against customer's dedicated endpoint (prod/us-east) using SDK v2 with streaming=true
Send a short prompt (e.g., 'Summarize: Redwood platform advantages')
Observe time between request and first streaming token; repeat ~50 times to surface distribution
Optionally toggle model pin to prior variant to compare (redwood-7b-quant-v1)
logs: serving-runtime: session_init_ms p50=1200 p90=8200 p99=11500 (post-cutover baseline pre-cutover p99=2200)
compiler: kernel_swap events spike at 2026-03-10T02:03:12Z concurrent_with model_loads=24
scheduler: batch_wait_ms increased from median 5ms to 320ms for dedicated pool nodes
kafka/metrics: routing_failures increased by 3x around cutover window
customer logs: client recorded stream handshake start then no bytes until 9–12s; multiple clients logged 'stream timed out after 30s' followed by auto-retry
investigation_notes: 03/10 03:15 UTC - Initial triage by Support: confirmed customer repro and captured traces; escalated to SRE and runtime on-call
03/10 04:00 UTC - SRE: checked node CPU/GPU metrics; no sustained GPU saturation but CPU-steal on some nodes during model loads
03/10 05:10 UTC - Runtime Eng: observed increased KV cache misses immediately after compiler swap, resulting in extra RT operations for prefix handling
03/10 06:30 UTC - Network: no packet loss on VPC level; TLS handshake times normal; hints point to in-process stall rather than external network
03/11 09:20 UTC - Hypothesis #1: kernel selection path introduced an extra synchronous I/O on first request to a freshly-loaded model which blocks streaming initiation
03/11 12:00 UTC - Hypothesis #2: scheduler batching threshold changed in compiler roll that increased initial batch wait time for low-QPS sessions in dedicated pools
03/12 14:00 UTC - Mitigation test: forced fallback to prior compiler runtime on a canary node; TTFB p99 dropped to ~2.4s on canary vs 10.9s on upgraded nodes
03/12 16:45 UTC - Correlation: incidents match nodes that experienced concurrent model cold loads plus kernel swap events
root_cause: A newly-introduced synchronous kernel initialization path in the compiler cutover caused blocking on the serving thread during first token emission when combined with concurrent model binary swaps and cold KV cache state. This increased batch wait times for small sessions and manifested as elevated TTFB and streaming timeouts for affected dedicated pool nodes.
resolution_summary: Rolled back the compiler change on the customer's dedicated pool nodes and applied a hotfix that converts the kernel init path to async+prefetch. After rollback and hotfix rollout to the pool, TTFB p99 returned to prior levels (~2s). Deployed canary test to validate fix before wide rollout. Customer notified and incident mitigation steps documented.
workaround: For immediate relief, we temporarily pinned the customer's dedicated pool to the previous runtime image (compiler-v1.14) and disabled eager kernel swap on low-QPS nodes. Customers on hosted tiers are unaffected by that pin. Documented steps provided to CS for reconfiguration.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-9123: Merge async kernel-init hotfix into main and schedule full rollout
SRE-1210: Add an alert for 'serving-runtime.session_init_ms p99 > 3s' for dedicated pools
DX-404: Update runbook with steps to pin runtime image and disable eager kernel swap
QA-678: Add regression tests that simulate concurrent model load + compiler swap with low-QPS sessions
comments: 2026-03-10 03:22 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports sudden regression after 02:00 UTC cutover; provided request IDs and example traces. Requested Priority escalation.
2026-03-10 04:05 - SRE (Arjun Patel): Captured node-level metrics and heap/CPU snapshots. No obvious OOMs; will instrument scheduler latencies.
2026-03-10 05:45 - Runtime Eng (Priya Rao): Reproduced locally using model pin and compiler combo; seeing blocking syscall during kernel selection. Investigating async conversion.

2026-03-11 12:05 - Support (Maya Chen): Applied temporary pin for the customer and observed immediate improvement; customer confirmed reduced timeouts. Moving to In Progress while eng completes patch.
2026-03-12 17:30 - Runtime Eng (Priya Rao): Hotfix pushed to canary; metrics look good. Preparing rollout plan and postmortem draft.
2026-03-13 09:10 - CS (Oliver Hughes): SlateDocs acknowledged workaround and requested timeline for full rollout and RCA; provided expected customer-facing communications timeline (48h).
